steps.say: A ballooned bile duct favours baby girls and often brings companion defects of the gut. A yellow infant girl with a belly lump earns a bile duct look.
steps.tx: A ballooned bile duct favours baby girls. **Choledochal cysts** (bile duct balloons) dilate the bile duct in **1 in 100000 to 150000 births** (one in one hundred thousand to one hundred fifty thousand births) with **3 to 4 fold** (three to four fold) **female preponderance** (girl excess) and links to duodenal and colonic atresia, imperforate anus and pancreas divisum as **associated anomalies** (paired defects). A jaundiced infant girl earns a bile duct look.

steps.say: Five shapes share one name, and the common bile duct balloon dominates every list. The liver only form with stones inside is its own entity.
steps.tx: Five shapes share one name. The **Todani classification** (cyst shape list) makes type I **50 to 80 percent** (fifty to eighty percent), type II diverticulum **2 percent** (two percent), type III **choledochocele** (bile duct mouth cyst) **1.4 to 4.5 percent** (one point four to four point five percent), type IV intra plus extrahepatic **15 to 35 percent** (fifteen to thirty five percent), and type V **Caroli disease** (liver only cysts) intrahepatic only in **20 percent** (twenty percent). Type I dominates every exam list.

vis.alt: Diagram of Caroli disease with dilated intrahepatic bile ducts, central dot sign and intraductal stones.
vis.caption: Type V disease with dilated intrahepatic ducts, central dot sign and stones. Type I extrahepatic ballooning is commoner. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A shared channel between bile and pancreas pipes explains the damage. Pancreatic juice flows backward, wakes up inside the bile duct and burns its wall.
steps.tx: A shared channel explains the damage. **Pancreaticobiliary malunion** (joined pipes) with a **common channel** (shared tube) over **6 mm** (six millimetres) lets activated enzymes reflux and inflame the duct wall with high bile amylase, offering the leading pathogenesis for **bile reflux** (backward enzyme flow). Separating the two drainages later stops the burn.

steps.say: The full textbook trio rarely shows up together, so do not wait for it. Two of the three still count, and babies and older children tell different stories.
steps.tx: The textbook trio is usually incomplete. The full **classic triad** (three sign set) of jaundice, right upper quadrant mass and pain occurs in under **20 percent** (twenty percent) though **85 percent** (eighty five percent) show at least two. Infants present with **obstructive jaundice** (blocked yellow) and an **abdominal mass** (belly lump) while older children bring intermittent pain, fever and jaundice. Two of three still counts.

steps.say: Each scan answers one question, starting with sound waves and ending with a full road map. The camera down the throat is seldom needed in children.
steps.tx: Each scan answers one question. **Ultrasound** (sound scan) shows a cyst separate from gallbladder, **HIDA scan** (bile tracer test) shows absent then delayed uptake with duodenal emptying, magnetic resonance maps the whole tree and pancreas as **MRCP** (bile MRI), and endoscopic retrograde study is rarely needed. Start with sound waves; map with MRI before cutting.

steps.say: Take the whole cyst out and replumb the liver, because leaving any wall behind invites cancer. Drainage without removal belongs to history.
steps.tx: Take the whole cyst out and replumb the liver. Prompt **complete excision** (whole cyst removal) with Roux en Y **hepaticojejunostomy** (liver to bowel join) is mandatory because retained cyst carries up to **6 percent** (six percent) **malignancy risk** (cancer danger), and unsafe dissection is enucleated rather than left behind. Drainage alone without excision is obsolete.

steps.say: The new join must stay open for life, so watch it with regular scans. Rising liver tests years later mean image the join first.
steps.tx: The join must stay open for life. Separating **biliary drainage** (bile path) and pancreatic drainage arrests the inflammatory drive under the malunion theory, and **surveillance** (planned checks) ultrasound watches for **anastomotic stricture** (join narrowing). Rising liver tests years later mean image the join first, since strictures creep in silently.

steps.say: Delay lets the cyst burst into the belly or stew into stones, infection and scars. Fever with pain and yellow skin means infected bile needing urgent drainage.
steps.tx: Delay punishes twice. Rupture causes **bile peritonitis** (bile in belly) and chronic inflammation brings stones as **cholelithiasis** (gallstones), **cholangitis** (infected bile) and strictures, so complications of delay reinforce early excision. Fever with pain and jaundice means infected bile, which needs antibiotics and urgent drainage before definitive repair.

vis.caption: Stagnant bile invites stones, infection and strictures. Fever with pain and jaundice means infected bile needing urgent drainage. Credit: StewardMD.
